A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same research framework. Both main texts and Appendices A-D are readable, including their equations and figures, and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SGD and generative-sampling simulations on Gaussian mixtures and MNIST-based distributions, including comparisons with original MNIST data in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations and adds bimodal-mixture, class-imbalance, FashionMNIST, and component-comparison results.

M1.justification: The shallow tied-weight DAE, denoising objective, and online SGD remain. Time conditioning changes from v1 Appendix A.4's input perturbation e_t z to independently trainable preactivation weights p_t v with a separate update in v2 Eqs. (3) and (6). v2 also tests freezing the skip connection.

E1.justification: v2 adds generation from original FashionMNIST t-shirt and dress images, a bimodal Gaussian target, and an imbalanced trimodal target with probabilities 1/2, 1/3, and 1/6. These expand the represented distributions and test scenarios beyond the retained balanced trimodal and MNIST experiments.

E2.justification: Figure 14 introduces a fixed, untrained skip-connection DAE with b = 0.75 as an internal comparator to the trained-skip model. The earlier ReLU/tanh comparisons remain; no external baseline algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 introduces projected Hellinger-distance evaluation and controlled tests with additional time grids, schedules, and fixed skip connections. For the retained trimodal examples, reported diffusion noise changes from 0 to 0.1 and the sampling grid changes from spacing 0.02 to N = 100. Appendix D.1 specifies stopping at 0.95 for Figure 7, conflicting with its caption's 0.98; the exact setting remains uncertain.

E4.justification: v2 adds explicit time-encoding comparisons of learning dynamics, generated densities, and Hellinger distance in Figures 11-13, plus schedule and skip-connection controls in Figure 14. Figure 9 tests adaptation to class imbalance. v1's brief qualitative assertions about time encoding did not provide these analyses.

E5.justification: The single-run disclosure in v1 Figure 6 remains in v2 Figure 5. Neither version reports confidence intervals, repeated-seed summaries, or significance tests. The new density-distance measurements do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New results show decreasing Hellinger distance during bimodal learning, adaptation to unequal mixture weights, variance loss on FashionMNIST, a small late-training benefit from time encoding, and altered density shapes under schedule/skip controls. The trimodal density plots are also replaced under changed reported settings, so their differences are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 extends the stated learning and transport characterization to trainable time-encoding weights, including new update equations and modified Gaussian expectations. Appendices A.7-A.8 add convergence analysis and a worked linear Gaussian-mixture case with proposed closed-form stationary parameters. Deep and attention architectures are additionally formulated as prospective extensions, not established results.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same central claims: asymptotic characterization of training and generated-density projections, architectural bias, and mode collapse leading to model collapse under synthetic retraining. The new evidence and revised title do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 proposes fixing the skip connection as a possible remedy for variance collapse and discusses how interpolation schedules influence this failure mode, while qualifying the evidence as preliminary. It also elaborates possible deep, attention, and wider-network extensions. The central architectural-bias explanation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds implementation details for Hellinger estimation: 5,000 generated samples, Gaussian KDE, and a 1,000-point grid over [-10, 10], with the procedure repeated for theoretical samples. Settings for the new controls are also supplied. The repository link, MNIST preprocessing, and manifold-density discretization instructions remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted connections to score-estimation/generalization work, feature localization, heavy-tailed data, and mode/model collapse. Appendix A.6 links prospective attention extensions to sequence multi-index research. The central positioning against sample-complexity bounds and earlier restricted DAE analyses remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, expands explanations of summary statistics and transport, and uses the new bimodal example in the main narrative while moving the trimodal discussion to Appendix D.2. Appendices A and D gain subsections, but the overall main-section sequence and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds density-distance, FashionMNIST, imbalance, and component-comparison plots. It combines v1's MNIST density and image figures into Figure 3, and relocates and redraws the trimodal figures as Figures 7-8. These substantially revise the visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Direct FashionMNIST generation, quantitative density distances, and explicit component controls strengthen empirical support beyond v1, while expanded explanations improve accessibility. However, the added analysis contains localized errors: Eq. (70) omits the time-encoding chain-rule factor, and Eq. (88) prints M = rho Q where the alignment argument requires M squared = rho Q. Together with the conflicting Figure 7 stopping times, these temper the gains in validation and clarity.
